ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic lung cancer to the heart

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with prior cardiac and oncologic history
salient_findings: ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3 on ECG
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Progressive dyspnea on exertion
History of multiple prior cardiac events
History of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium
Received 2 drug-eluting stents to the right coronary artery 10 months prior
Denies chest pain at presentation
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin-T level was 40 ng/L
ECG shows normal sinus rhythm at 90 beats per minute
ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1, V2, and V3
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows well-circumscribed mass in the left ventricular mid-apical anteroseptum
Preserved left ventricular systolic function on echocardiogram
Large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade on echocardiogram
Coronary angiography shows nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of lung cancer with metastatic disease to the brain and myocardium, and the echocardiogram shows a large pericardial effusion with signs of impending cardiac tamponade, which is more consistent with malignant pericardial effusion than acute coronary syndrome.
raw.anchor_refutation: The patient's presentation and test results do not support acute coronary syndrome as the primary diagnosis, given the lack of chest pain, nonobstructive epicardial coronary artery disease, and the presence of a large pericardial effusion.

rejected.label: Constrictive pericarditis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and test results do not support constrictive pericarditis, which typically involves thickening of the pericardium and restrictive filling of the heart.
